title: Logic Optimization Meets SAT: A Novel Framework for Circuit-SAT Solving
problem: Circuit Satisfiability (CSAT) problems are critical in IC design and verification but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit structure intrinsics. Direct CSAT conversion to CNF loses structural information that could accelerate solving.
method: The framework integrates advanced logic synthesis techniques with reinforcement learning to preprocess CSAT instances before solving. A cost-customized Look-Up Table (LUT) mapping strategy prioritizes solver efficiency by transforming circuits into simplified forms tailored for SAT solvers. An RL agent optimizes the mapping strategy for the target instance, learning which transformations yield fastest solutions.

title: Architecting Space Microdatacenters: A System-level Approach
problem: There is no principled cost-aware methodology for architecting server-based computing systems deployed on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites (Space Microdatacenters, SuDC). Prior work proposes the concept but does not model Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) to guide hardware design decisions.
method: The authors build a TCO model for SuDC that decomposes costs into compute power, mass, monetary hardware cost, and communication. They perform a design space exploration over heterogeneous accelerator configurations (high FLOPs/W devices), collaborative compute constellations (EO satellites with onboard accelerators), monolithic vs. distributed architectures, and compute overprovisioning strategies. TCO sensitivity analysis reveals power dominates sublinearly; monetary cost and mass are secondary.

title: POLARIS: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Mitigating Power Side-Channel Leakage
problem: Microelectronic systems handling sensitive data (encryption keys) are vulnerable to power side-channel attacks that infer secrets through dynamic power profiles; current mitigation solutions suffer from high overhead or incomplete leakage reduction.
method: POLARIS framework uses Explainable AI (XAI) to guide a masking-based mitigation approach. Employs unsupervised process to automatically build tailored training datasets without manual labeling. Trains a masking model on this dataset to obfuscate power signatures. XAI guidance enables targeting the most exploitable power patterns for efficient mitigation.

title: 23.5 MAE: A 3nm 0.168mm2 576MAC Mini AutoEncoder with Line-Based Depth-First Scheduling for Generative AI in Vision on Edge Devices
problem: Deploying generative vision models (diffusion) on edge devices requires running autoencoders efficiently within tight area/power budgets; limited on-chip memory forces high DRAM access (40–80% of energy cost) and on-chip memory constraints cause temporal under-utilization of MAC units.
method: MAE is a 3nm domain-specific tiny NPU integrating 576 MACs in 0.168 mm² using line-based depth-first fusion with branch-handling to minimize external memory access (EMA). Local H-reuse caching exploits inter-layer data locality; direct links bypass redundant dataflow stages. Global scheduling framework optimizes latency and EMA jointly across the autoencoder graph.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper RedSan: A Redundant Memory Instruction Sanitizer for GPU Programs
problem: Artifact evaluation for SC25 reproducibility report on GPU memory instruction sanitization.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 reproducibility guidelines.

title: Decoupling Analog Circuit Representation from Technology for Behavior-Centric Optimization
problem: Analog IC design is strongly coupled with technology nodes and difficult to represent via abstract behavioral models; lack of accurate and efficient analog modeling hampers design automation, especially when porting designs across technologies.
method: Proposes behavior-centric optimization framework representing circuit behavior via transistor electrical properties rather than sizes, improving generalization across technologies; develops method mapping electrical properties to device sizes; uses radial basis functions-based Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RBF-KAN) to approximate nonlinear circuit behavior with limited simulations.

title: 24.8 A 12GS/s 9b 16× Time-Interleaved SAR ADC in 16nm FinFET
problem: RF direct sampling and phased-array applications require high-speed ADCs (>GS/s) with both high sample rate and high SNDR (>45dB), but existing designs often require multiple supply domains or complex integration schemes.
method: 16-channel time-interleaved SAR ADC architecture operating at 12GS/s with 16nm FinFET technology, using integration-friendly single 1.8V and 0.8V supply domains optimized for area and power efficiency.

title: DPUaudit: DPU-assisted Pull-based Architecture for Near-Zero Cost System Auditing
problem: Existing hardware-based system auditing frameworks offload log processing to isolated hardware but still suffer high runtime overhead (>10% slowdown) because they use a push-based architecture requiring a log sender to run on the monitored host, which necessitates heavy software protection mechanisms that consume significant CPU resources.
method: DPUaudit replaces the push-based log sender on the monitored host with a pull-based architecture using a DPU (Data Processing Unit/SmartNIC) to actively pull system events directly from the monitored host's memory over the network interconnect. By removing the log sender from the monitored host entirely, DPUaudit eliminates the need for complex software protection mechanisms guarding it, achieving near-zero overhead. The DPU handles log collection, processing, and integrity verification in an isolated SmartNIC environment, physically separated from the monitored host.

title: An Experimental Demonstration of Neuronal Somatic Behavior Using 2D SnS Memristive Switching Characteristics and its Equivalent Circuit for Spiking Neural Network
problem: This report presents the fabrication and characterization of a 2D SnS memristor, proposing its integrate and fire (I&F) model as a potential hardware implementation of neuronal somatic behavior
method: designed and its response has been shown to emulate the experimentally demonstrated somatic behavior, that can be used for neuromorphic circuit designs

title: Extending MPI Correctness Benchmarking to the Fortran Language
problem: MPI correctness benchmarks (test suites for MPI implementations) exist for C but not Fortran, despite MPI standard supporting both languages; Fortran MPI code quality assessment incomplete
method: Porting MPI-BugBench (most recent MPI correctness benchmark) test generation logic to Fortran; identification of language-specific porting challenges; comparative accuracy evaluation of MUST (dynamic MPI correctness tool) on C and Fortran

title: DReX: Accurate and Scalable Dense Retrieval Acceleration via Algorithmic-Hardware Codesign
problem: Approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) used in RAG dense retrieval is dataset-specific and inherently low-recall, causing irrelevant or incomplete context to degrade LLM generation quality. Exact nearest-neighbor search is too compute- and bandwidth-intensive for conventional processors.
method: DReX combines two hardware tiers: in-DRAM logic performs early filtering by comparing query vectors against embedding centroids to eliminate distant candidates without moving full vectors off-chip, and an outside-DRAM near-memory accelerator then executes exact k-NN search on the filtered, much smaller candidate set. The in-DRAM filter exploits processing-in-memory (PIM) capabilities of commodity DRAM to compute approximate distance bounds, bypassing DRAM-to-processor transfers for the bulk of vectors. This two-stage pipeline minimizes off-chip data movement while guaranteeing exact retrieval on the survivors.

title: Enhancing LLM-based Quantum Code Generation with Multi-Agent Optimization and Quantum Error Correction
problem: LLM-based quantum code generation struggles with fault-tolerance and correctness; general-purpose LLM techniques (CoT, RAG) don't translate to quantum domain without domain-specific optimization.
method: Multi-agent framework where each agent targets specific quantum optimizations (error correction, circuit synthesis); semantic analyzer with multi-pass inference; integrates structured Chain-of-Thought and error correction decoder; test suite measuring per-agent contribution.

title: CXL-INTERPLAY: Unraveling and Characterizing CXL Interference in Modern Computer Systems
problem: Compute Express Link (CXL) enables memory/storage expansion but faces performance degradation when coexisting with conventional memory and storage systems; interference effects are largely unexplored in real hardware, creating blind spots in deployment.
method: CXL-Interplay systematically characterizes and analyzes interference from memory and storage systems on CXL using real CXL hardware. Employs performance counter analysis and kernel-level tracing for reverse-reasoning investigation of interference mechanisms. Proposes and evaluates mitigation solutions to reduce identified interference.

title: 4.2 A 1.8-to-3.0GHz Fully Integrated All-In-One CMOS Frequency Management Module Achieving -47/+42ppm Inaccuracy from -40 to 95°C and -150/+70ppm After Accelerated Aging
problem: Wireless/wired communication systems require stable frequency references, traditionally using bulky off-chip crystals. On-chip RC-based references struggle with poor aging performance (>±1030 ppm drift after aging even with redundancy) and inadequate frequency accuracy for modern protocols; integrating on-chip reference into synthesizer for true FMM remains unachieved.
method: Fully integrated frequency management module (FMM) combines on-chip frequency reference (RC-based with improved stability techniques) and frequency synthesizer in single CMOS chip. Covers 1.8–3.0 GHz output range; achieves ±47/±42 ppm inaccuracy across -40 to +95°C (far superior to prior RC-core designs). Post-aging specs: ±150/±70 ppm after accelerated testing.

title: The Cost of Teaching Operational ML
problem: Operational ML requires skills beyond model development, including infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation—capabilities grounded in HPC and distributed systems but lacking comprehensive educational frameworks.
method: Graduate-level course (ML Systems Engineering and Operations) using Chameleon Cloud testbed for hands-on infrastructure provisioning, distributed training, deployment, monitoring, and automation across 186,692 compute instance hours.

title: 7.9 A 60Gb/s NRZ Burst-Mode CDR with Cross-Injection Locking and Flash Phase Detector Achieving 0.13ns Reconfiguration Time in 28nm CMOS
problem: Rapidly reconfigurable photonic switch networks operating at ns-scale require burst-mode clock and data recovery (BM-CDR) with sub-ns reconfiguration time, but prior injection-locking BM-CDRs suffer from poor jitter at higher data rates.
method: 60Gb/s burst-mode CDR using cross-injection-locking technique to suppress recovered-clock jitter, combined with a flash phase detector (PD) that extracts phase information between data and sampling clock within 2UI, achieving 0.13ns reconfiguration time in 28nm CMOS.
